This page describes JQL functions that help you search across Jira issue hierarchies. You can use these functions to find parent issues, child issues, or recursive relationships between issues in both the standard Jira hierarchy and Advanced Roadmaps hierarchy levels. These functions are useful when building filters, reports, or searches that depend on issue relationships rather than individual issue attributes.

With the latest update, these advanced extensions are now embedded in Jira's built-in search, allowing users to access detailed information without disrupting their existing workflow.

By acting as a translation layer, the application transforms custom functions into native Jira JQL queries. This facilitates seamless integration for complex searches involving hierarchies, linked issues, or specific comments.

Users can now enter functions directly in the standard Jira search interface, eliminating the need to toggle between applications. Furthermore, any resulting queries can be saved as filters, following standard Jira protocols.

The use cases on this page provide examples of using JQL Search Extensions with Dashboard Hub, a leading Appfire reporting and dashboard solution.

Dashboard Hub is an all-in-one Jira dashboard app for building reports that keep teams informed. Nearly every gadget can be driven by a JQL query, so any filter, keyword, or function you use from JQL Search Extensions (JSE) works inside a Dashboard Hub gadget with no extra setup. Combining Dashboard Hub with JQL Search Extensions means you can report on relationships, comments, and content that standard Jira can’t surface.

content.text: Why use JQL Search Extensions and Dashboard Hub together
Report on more of your data
: JSE can retrieve work items by their links, comments, attachments, and hierarchy. Feeding those queries or filters into a gadget lets you chart data that native Jira gadgets simply can’t reach.
: Save an extended search once and reuse it across pie charts, tables, and stats. Every gadget refresh re-runs the full query, so your dashboards stay current on their own.
Clearer picture for the whole team
: Turning complex searches into simple visuals gives team leads and stakeholders an at-a-glance view of blockers, progress, and workload without writing a single query themselves.
: Describe what you want to find in plain language with JSE’s AI search, save it as a filter, and drop it into a gadget. There’s no development work and no manual data pulling.
What scenarios benefit from this integration
Our gadgets serve an extensive range of industries and teams. Here are a few examples where our customers are implementing the real-life use cases presented in this section:
: Dashboards can visualize blockers and linked-work item dependencies across Epics, Stories, and Subtasks, keeping engineering, QA, and product teams aligned on what’s holding up delivery.
: Scrum Masters and product owners get live charts of sprint readiness and progress across every epic, without rebuilding reports each sprint.
: Filters that track who last commented let support leads chart response coverage and spot issues awaiting a reply.
: Interconnected workstreams become easy to monitor when linked-work item filters feed a single dashboard, reducing the risk of overlooked dependencies.
: Filters that search attachment content surface work items tied to specific documents or clauses, giving teams a shared, always-current view for audits and reviews.

Self-serve reindexing options for stuck index issues

Jira administrators can now trigger reindexing directly from the indexing progress bar when  indexing is stuck. To help prevent unnecessary reindexing, this option is available once every three months.
Depending on your instance, JQL Search Extensions displays one of the following options:
– Available when your instance contains more than 10,000 issues or more than 25% of issues are unindexed.
– Available when your instance contains fewer than 10,000 and fewer than 25% of issues are unindexed.
